item.title: Eight US States Sue OpenAI, Alleging ChatGPT Endangered Children for Profit (2026)
item.description:
The attorneys general of eight US states have filed lawsuits against OpenAI, alleging that the ChatGPT maker deceived and endangered the public, particularly children, in the name of profit.

West Virginia, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana announced the complaints on October 14, according to the filings published by the states.

The lawsuits target AI safety practices at the company behind ChatGPT, and OpenAI has not issued a public response to the complaints.

What the State Complaints Allege Against OpenAI

The complaints allege that ChatGPT has "coached" users to harm themselves and others. The West Virginia filing states that a growing body of research indicates ChatGPT is degrading critical thinking skills, encouraging paranoias and delusions, offering dangerous medical advice, and promoting unhealthy behaviors and relationships.

Recent reports of "rogue" AI agents at OpenAI are presented as evidence of recklessness. "All these harms were foreseeable and avoidable," the West Virginia complaint reads.

The filing argues that CEO Sam Altman has warned about the safety risks of AI since at least 2015, that it is no secret children use ChatGPT, and that OpenAI employees have left the company over safety concerns.

OpenAI acknowledged last year that its systems can "fall short" when responding to users in distress, while saying it has "a stack of layered safeguards" in place.

The company also states on its website that it uses age prediction to place some users in a teen-oriented ChatGPT experience with additional safeguards, unless those users verify that they are adults.

California Class Action Targets Children's Data

A separate class action lawsuit was filed in California on Tuesday on behalf of two children and "all other children similarly situated." The suit alleges that OpenAI deliberately used ChatGPT to extract personal information from children and profited from that information by using it to train its models.

Altman's own words form part of that case. The complaint cites his comment on a podcast last year that people share the most personal details of their lives with ChatGPT, and that young people in particular use it as a therapist or life coach.

Under California law, the complaint asserts, an adult cannot collect and monetize that kind of information from a child and then claim the child authorized it. The lawsuits add to regulatory pressure on AI developers over user data, following the UK ICO data protection commitments from AI developers announced last week.

Nothing changes for ChatGPT users right away. Parents whose children use ChatGPT can check whether an account has been placed in the teen experience, which OpenAI says applies additional safeguards, and review what personal information the child has shared in conversations. Adults placed in the teen experience by mistake can verify their age to leave it.

The complaints are at an early stage, and no court has ruled on any of the allegations. OpenAI has not said whether it will change ChatGPT's safeguards for younger users in response.

item.title: Riot Will Shut Down League of Legends Classic in January 2027 and Refund Obsolete Content (2027)
item.description:
Riot Games will shut down League of Legends Classic in January 2027, the company announced in a developer update on the official League of Legends website.

The current Classic season will be the last, and Riot says it will refund Classic content made obsolete by the closure. According to a Riot spokesperson, players had fun revisiting the older version of the game with Classic, but "at this point though, most have gone back to other parts of League."

Classic will keep receiving content until the closure, but no new season is planned after the current one. League of Legends Classic was built around nostalgia for the older era of the game.

The mode removed most champions and kits introduced since 2013, brought back an older version of the Summoner's Rift map, and promised to add "new" old champions faster than the original game did. Riot has not given an exact January date for the shutdown.

Riot's Plans for League of Legends Classic After the Shutdown

The mode is not being deleted for good. "We'll then put Classic back in the box for now, with the goal of bringing it back, likely as an event mode with adjustments and additions," Riot says.

The company also plans to share more about what it learned from this run, including where it thinks it got Classic right, where it could have gone "more classic," and where sticking too closely to the past held the experience back.

Riot described the mode as "a true labor of love" for its developers, thanked players who asked for it on social media and voted in the Council, and said it will keep exploring different ways to play League.

Remaining Champions and Refunds Before Classic Closes

Classic still has content coming before it goes offline. At least seven more champions are scheduled to arrive in the mode:

  • Mordekaiser, Yorick, Hecarim, and Lucian in the upcoming 26.21 update
  • Volibear, Urgot, and Udyr in later updates

Players who bought Classic content have little to do right now. Riot says refunds will be issued for Classic content rendered obsolete by the closure, but the update does not explain which items qualify, how the refunds will be paid out, or when they will be processed.

Players who still enjoy the mode have until January to play the final season, including the champions added in 26.21. Anyone weighing a purchase of Classic content in the meantime should keep the shutdown date in mind, since the mode ends in January 2027 regardless of when the item was bought.

Riot has not said when Classic could return as an event mode or which changes that version would include.

item.title: WhatsApp Rolls Out Guest Calling So People Without an Account Can Join Calls From a Browser (2026)
item.description:
Meta has started rolling out guest calling in WhatsApp, a feature that lets people without a WhatsApp account join a WhatsApp call through an invite link.

The company announced the change on Wednesday in a post on the WhatsApp blog. Guests join from a computer browser and always need an invitation from an existing WhatsApp user, since they cannot start calls of their own.

Meta says guest calls keep the core properties of regular WhatsApp calls. They are free, and they are end-to-end encrypted, so bringing someone from outside the platform into a conversation does not lower its privacy level.

Until now, every participant in a WhatsApp call needed a WhatsApp account. That requirement made group calls awkward whenever one or two people in a group relied on a different messaging app.

How WhatsApp Guest Calling Works and What Guests Cannot Do

Guests are deliberately limited. Each guest needs approval from the call host and sits in a waiting room until the host lets them in. The host can also remove a guest from the call at any time.

Meta lists these restrictions for people who join without an account:

  • no visibility of other participants' phone numbers
  • no option to send messages during the call
  • no option to add other people to the call
  • no option to create a new call

Guests still have some tools. They can share their screen, react with emojis, and raise their hand. Guest calling works for one-on-one calls as well as group calls with up to 32 participants.

Inviting someone who does not use WhatsApp is handled from the Calls tab:

  1. Open WhatsApp and switch to the Calls tab.
  2. Tap the plus (+) button and create a call link.
  3. Send the link to the person who does not have a WhatsApp account.
  4. The guest opens the link in a computer browser and enters a name.
  5. Admit the guest from the waiting room when the call starts.

Why Guest Calling Matters for WhatsApp Users

Host approval is the main safeguard in the new system. Anyone holding a call link can reach the waiting room, so hosts should check names before admitting guests, particularly when a link has been forwarded beyond the original recipient.

The hidden phone numbers protect existing participants from exposing their contact details to someone they do not know.

WhatsApp is not the first calling service to take this route. Apple's FaceTime already lets users create call links that people on Android, Windows, or Linux devices can join The WhatsApp change follows another recent account policy update, after the service started to block logins on outdated operating systems.

Meta's announcement describes guests joining from a computer browser and does not say whether mobile browsers are supported. WhatsApp users who do not see the call link option yet should update the app to the latest version.

item.title: Google Removes Gemini Pro Models From the $4.99 AI Plus Plan Starting November 13 (2026)
item.description:
Google will remove access to Gemini Pro models from its $4.99 per month Google AI Plus subscription on November 13, 2026, according to an email the Google One team is sending to AI Plus subscribers. From that date, selecting Pro models in the Gemini app and in AI Mode in Google Search will be limited to Google AI Pro subscribers and higher tiers.

AI Plus is the cheapest paid Google AI plan. It has been sold with access to faster Gemini models and 400GB of Google storage, and Pro model access was one of its main selling points for subscribers who wanted more than the free tier.

Google says AI Plus subscribers will keep access to its latest Flash-Lite model and to Flash, which the company describes as built for speed and intelligence. Existing conversations that used a Pro model are not deleted. Those chats can be continued after November 13, but with a different model.

Why Google Is Moving Pro Models to Higher Tiers

The change was signaled earlier. When Google rolled out Gemini 4 Argon, the company said the new model would only be available on AI Pro and AI Ultra plans, not AI Plus.

Google also said at the time that AI Plus subscribers would later lose access to all Gemini Pro models. The November 13 email puts a date on that plan. After the change, Google's AI plans line up as follows:

  • Free: Gemini Flash-Lite
  • AI Plus ($4.99 per month): Gemini Flash-Lite and Gemini Flash
  • AI Pro ($19.99 per month): everything in AI Plus, plus Gemini Pro models and Gemini 4 Argon
  • AI Ultra 5x ($99.99 per month): AI Pro features with higher Pro model access and 5x higher usage limits
  • AI Ultra 20x ($199.99 per month): AI Ultra 5x features with 20x higher usage limits and the highest Pro model access

For AI Plus subscribers, the practical result is a gap of $15 per month between the plan they pay for and the cheapest plan that keeps Pro models. Google points subscribers to a Help Center article for details and says the subscription can be managed or canceled at any time.

Subscribers who rely on Pro models have a little under a month to decide how to respond:

  1. Review the Google One plan comparison page to see which models, limits, and storage each tier includes.
  2. Test whether Gemini Flash handles typical prompts well enough, since Flash remains part of AI Plus.
  3. Finish or export important work from Pro model conversations before November 13, when those chats switch to another model.
  4. Upgrade to AI Pro, keep AI Plus, or cancel through Google One, depending on how much Pro model access matters.

The trade-off is straightforward. Staying on AI Plus keeps the lower price and the storage, while Pro models and Gemini 4 Argon now require the $19.99 AI Pro plan.

The email does not mention a price change for AI Plus or any change to the plan's 400GB of storage, and Google has not said whether existing subscribers will receive any compensation for losing Pro model access.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Google Removes Gemini Pro Models From the $4.99 AI Plus Plan Starting November 13 appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: OpenAI Accuses a Former Employee of Taking More Than 100 Confidential Hardware Files Back to Apple (2026)
item.description:
OpenAI has accused a former employee of taking more than 100 confidential files about its unreleased hardware back to Apple, according to a court filing OpenAI submitted on Wednesday in the trade secrets case Apple brought against the company.

OpenAI claims the employee, who joined from Apple and returned to Apple six months later, transferred sensitive documents to personal accounts before leaving.

The filing does not name the employee. OpenAI has asked the court for time to investigate the matter and to consider counterclaims against Apple.

OpenAI's Allegations Against Apple in the Trade Secrets Case

According to the filing, the files included:

  • detailed images of at least one unreleased OpenAI device
  • engineering and manufacturing data
  • supplier information and project files
  • specifications for cosmetic finishes
  • reports on coating and sealing hardware components

OpenAI says some of the files were transferred just after midnight in Singapore on June 2, which the filing describes as the employee's final day at OpenAI.

The filing goes further than the alleged file transfer. OpenAI claims the former employee presented OpenAI's product plans to Apple's senior leadership, including Apple's vice president of operations in Asia.

According to OpenAI, that presentation took place months ago. OpenAI now points to Apple's latest AI hardware push, including its newly announced smart home products such as Apple's $299 HomeView smart display, as a reason for concern.

OpenAI told the court it is worried that its confidential information is now circulating inside Apple, where engineers could use it to shape upcoming Apple products.

Apple rejects the claims. The company says it has found nothing to support OpenAI's allegations and that it has rules that stop employees from bringing former employers' secrets into Apple.

How the Apple and OpenAI Trade Secrets Dispute Started

The new filing reverses the direction of the original case. In July, Apple sued OpenAI and two former Apple employees, Chang Liu and Tang Yew Tan, alleging that the pair took confidential engineering information, including details about unreleased products, to help OpenAI develop its own hardware.

OpenAI denied those accusations at the time, saying it had no interest in other companies' trade secrets. With the new filing, OpenAI argues that confidential hardware information may have moved from OpenAI to Apple instead. OpenAI has not yet shown that Apple received or used any of the files it says were taken.

For consumers, the dispute has no immediate effect on existing Apple or OpenAI products. It does show that both companies are developing AI hardware in parallel, with OpenAI working on at least one unreleased device and Apple expanding into AI-powered smart home products.

Anyone following either company's hardware plans should watch the court docket for counterclaims, which would turn OpenAI's defense into a direct case against Apple.

OpenAI has not filed any counterclaims yet, and the filing does not say when its investigation into the transferred files will be complete.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post OpenAI Accuses a Former Employee of Taking More Than 100 Confidential Hardware Files Back to Apple appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Rockstar Releases the GTA 6 Launch Trailer Ahead of the November 19 Console Release (2026)
item.description:
Rockstar Games has released the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6, its final trailer before the game arrives on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

The company shared the video on October 15 and says it features the debut of "Flower in a Hurricane," a new track from GTA 6 score composers Justice featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. The song will appear on the official GTA 6 soundtrack album.

The music choice breaks with the previous GTA 6 trailers. The first trailer used Tom Petty's "Love Is a Long Road," and the second used "Hot Together" by The Pointer Sisters. Both were licensed songs, while the launch trailer uses original music written for the game.

What the GTA 6 Launch Trailer Shows

The trailer focuses on the two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, more than earlier footage did. Jason appears with long hair for much of the video and talks about the obstacles he faced after leaving the military under less-than-glamorous circumstances. Lucia is shown wearing a monitoring anklet, and at one point she asks whether the two of them are going to be OK.

Helicopters play a large part in the action scenes:

  • a helicopter crashes behind Jason while he carries an assault rifle
  • Lucia rides in another helicopter through the city with a grenade launcher
  • a third helicopter swings a chained load of cargo through a row of windows on a building

The trailer ends with Jason and Lucia jumping off a roof into a hotel pool.

Rockstar's official video description sums up the story setup. Jason and Lucia have always known the odds are against them, and when an easy score goes wrong, they end up in a criminal conspiracy that stretches across the state of Leonida, forced to rely on each other to survive.

The launch trailer passed 1 million views on YouTube in about half an hour. It was captured on PlayStation 5, and PlayStation branding appears at the start and end of the video.

GTA 6 Release Details and the Missing PC Version

Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. Console players who want to watch the trailer can find it on Rockstar's official YouTube channel, and the full version of "Flower in a Hurricane" is available there as well.

PC players have nothing to plan for yet. Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6 or given it a release date, and Microsoft has already said that the game will not be playable on PC through the cloud. PC players should not expect a launch day version on that platform.

Rockstar has not shared further trailers or a PC announcement alongside the launch trailer, and the November 19 date currently applies only to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Rockstar Releases the GTA 6 Launch Trailer Ahead of the November 19 Console Release appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Confirms Windows 11 KB5127648 Update Can Block Users From Turning On Smart App Control (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has confirmed that the October KB5127648 security update for Windows 11 can prevent some users from turning on Smart App Control, according to an update to the official KB5127648 support document.

On affected devices running Windows 11 version 24H2 and later, the Smart App Control option in the Windows Security app is grayed out and cannot be toggled.

A permanent fix is not available yet. Microsoft has published two temporary workarounds, one based on the registry and one based on Group Policy, aimed mainly at IT administrators who manage enterprise devices.

Which Windows 11 Devices Are Affected by the Smart App Control Bug

Smart App Control is a Windows 11 security feature that uses Microsoft's app intelligence services and code integrity features. It works alongside Microsoft Defender and SmartScreen to block apps or binaries that may be harmful.

The problem only hits systems where the feature was switched off before the update. "After installing this update, some devices might be unable to turn on Smart App Control in the Windows Security app if it has been turned off," Microsoft says in the advisory. The company adds that devices where Smart App Control is already turned on are not affected and remain protected.

Users who never planned to enable Smart App Control will not notice any change. The bug matters for anyone who wants to switch the protection on after installing the October update, a step that is blocked on affected systems.

Microsoft's Registry and Group Policy Workarounds

Microsoft's registry workaround restores the toggle on affected devices. It requires administrator rights and a restart:

  1. Type cmd in the Windows Search box.
  2. Select Run as Administrator to open an elevated Command Prompt window.
  3. Enter reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Policies\Microsoft\FeatureManagement\Overrides" /v 2883193997 /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f and press Enter.
  4. Enter reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Policies\Microsoft\FeatureManagement\Overrides" /v 2850574478 /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f and press Enter.
  5. Restart the device, then open the Windows Security app and turn on Smart App Control.

Administrators of managed fleets can install two Group Policy packages instead. Microsoft lists them as KB5074105 261015_19222 Feature Preview and KB5074105 261015_19221 Feature Preview, both covering Windows 11 versions 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2.

Once installed, the policies appear under Computer Configuration, Administrative Templates, the Group Policy name, and then Windows 11, version 24H2, 25H2.

Both settings must be set to Enabled, and the affected devices need a restart before the change applies. The policies also turn on logging for troubleshooting.

The Smart App Control issue is the latest in a series of confirmed problems with recent Windows 11 updates. Earlier this week, Microsoft also resolved a separate bug behind black screens and Explorer crashes after sign-in, and it acknowledged Remote Desktop failures for non-admin users when the Administrator protection feature is enabled.

Microsoft has not said when a fix for the Smart App Control toggle will ship, and the registry and Group Policy changes remain temporary measures until that update arrives.

item.title: Google Rolls Out Gmail AI Inbox to Paid Workspace Users in the US, With Wider Rollout From October 26 (2026)
item.description:
Google is rolling out AI Inbox in Gmail to paid Google Workspace customers, according to an official Google Workspace Updates announcement. The feature, first introduced in January, is limited at launch to users in the United States whose account language is set to US English.

AI Inbox goes further than the single-thread Gemini summaries that Gmail has offered for the past year. Instead of waiting for a user to open an email and request a recap, Gmail scans incoming messages and builds a live briefing of deadlines and status updates.

How Gmail's AI Inbox Works

AI Inbox does not replace the traditional chronological inbox. Google places it as a separate view in the Gmail navigation menu, both in the desktop web client and in the mobile app, and it centers on two views:

  • Suggested to-dos, which pull action items, deliverables, and due dates out of long email chains.
  • Topics to catch up on, which group rapid replies and multi-message project discussions into summaries that highlight the latest decisions and status changes.

Workspace administrators do not need to change anything in the Admin console. The view appears automatically in the Gmail menu for eligible users. Google describes the launch as requiring zero admin setup.

For users, the practical change is that tasks buried in a thread no longer have to be copied by hand into a separate notes or to-do app.

Gmail AI Inbox Rollout Schedule and Eligible Workspace Plans

Google is staggering the deployment across Workspace domains over the coming weeks:

  1. Rapid Release domains started receiving AI Inbox on October 12, 2026, and full visibility can take up to 15 days.
  2. Scheduled Release domains begin a gradual 15-day rollout on October 26, 2026.

At launch, AI Inbox is available to Business Standard, Business Plus, Enterprise Standard, Enterprise Plus, and Frontline Plus subscribers. Google says Business Starter, Enterprise Starter, and AI Pro for Education accounts will get the feature over the next few months.

Workspace users who do not see AI Inbox yet should check two things: whether their account language is set to US English, and whether their domain is on the Rapid Release or Scheduled Release track.

Users on the Scheduled Release track will not get the view before October 26. Accounts on the same plan can receive it at different times during the rollout window.

Google has not announced when AI Inbox will expand to additional languages or markets outside the United States.

item.title: Brave Adds End-to-End Encryption to Leo AI Chats Using a Trusted Execution Environment (2026)
item.description:
Brave Software has connected the Leo AI assistant in its browser to Z.ai's GLM 5.3 Flash model with end-to-end encryption, running the model inside a trusted execution environment (TEE) operated by NEAR AI.

The company says the setup keeps the content of AI conversations hidden from Brave and the identity of the person asking hidden from NEAR AI. The launch follows an experiment Brave started in November 2025 to create a confidential channel for AI conversations in Leo using NEAR AI's TEE.

How Brave Encrypts Leo Conversations

A prompt sent to Leo in this mode is encrypted on the device and sent over the network with Oblivious HTTP, a protocol that separates network requests from their content. Brave's AI Gateway then forwards the encrypted query to the TEE without passing along the user's IP address.

Before sending anything, the browser verifies the enclave's attestation and encrypts the query with a key bound to the TEE. The enclave decrypts the request, runs it through GLM 5.3 Flash, and returns an encrypted answer that only the receiving browser can decrypt.

NEAR AI's confidential pipeline is built on Intel TDX and Nvidia Confidential Compute. Data isolation prevents the prompt or the response from being read during processing, and responses are signed inside the TEE. Attestation lets users confirm that the model has not been swapped for a different one.

Leo can still run web searches in this setup. Those searches go through the Brave Search API's LLM context endpoint from inside the TEE, not from the user's browser, which keeps the user's IP address out of the request.

"AI has raised the stakes, yet too much of it still runs on 'trust me bro' promises, often at the user's expense," Brave co-founder and CEO Brendan Eich said in a statement published by NEAR AI.

Why Encrypted AI Chats Matter for Brave Users

AI agents such as Meta's Muse ask for extensive access to personal information, and some AI companies repurpose conversations for model training. The Brave approach is meant to make the privacy claim verifiable through attestation instead of relying on a provider's zero data retention promise.

Apple, AWS, Google, Nvidia, and Microsoft all operate some form of private cloud compute for AI. Running an open weight model on local hardware remains another way to keep prompts off third-party servers.

Brave users who want this protection need to use Leo with the GLM 5.3 Flash model, since the end-to-end encrypted path covers that model inside the NEAR AI enclave.

The implementation is not complete. Brave plans to move the attestation check into the browser itself, publish a log of TEE keys, and provide enclave attestation for the exact model weights loaded into memory, and the company has not given a timeline for those steps.

item.title: Valve Adds Steam Achievement Sets That Keep DLC From Lowering Base Game Completion (2026)
item.description:
Valve has added achievement sets to the Steam client beta, a change that lets developers group achievements and keep DLC and seasonal achievements separate from a game's base list, according to Valve's official Steam client beta announcement.

The update also redesigns the achievements page and adds side-by-side comparisons with friends. The system is currently limited to the Steam Client Beta.

Developers can create sets tailored to a game, for example for mastering a specific character class or finishing a singleplayer campaign. Sets also mark which achievements belong to the base game and which belong to separate DLC or seasonal content.

What Changes for Steam Achievement Completion

Under the old system, a game with every achievement unlocked showed 100% in the achievements list. When a developer released DLC with new achievements, that figure dropped, even for players who never planned to buy or play the expansion. With sets, DLC achievements no longer pull down the base game's completion percentage, as long as the developer uses the new system.

Seasonal content works the same way. Valve's example is a set called "Halloween Event Achievements" that is valid for a limited period and does not affect the base game's achievement count. Players who skip a season keep their base game stats intact, which also fits games with battle passes.

The redesigned achievements page now shows most information on a single screen, including overall completion progress and progress toward individual achievements.

Players can also compare achievements with up to three friends at once. Separate DLC trophy lists and friend comparisons have been available on PlayStation consoles for some time.

Games That Support Steam Achievement Sets

Not every Steam game uses achievement sets yet. The following titles already support them:

  • Against the Storm, Age of Wonders 4, and Crusader Kings III
  • American Truck Simulator and Euro Truck Simulator 2
  • Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and Forza Horizon 5
  • DREDGE, Flock Around, and He is Coming
  • LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
  • Left 4 Dead 2, Portal 2, and Team Fortress 2
  • PowerWash Simulator and PowerWash Simulator 2
  • Victoria 3

Players who want achievement sets now have to sign up for the Steam Client Beta in the Steam client. Everyone else can wait for the stable release, which does not require any action.

Completionists who track 100% runs should check whether their games appear in the supported list before relying on the new percentages, because titles without sets still count DLC achievements toward the base total.

Beta features can still change before release. Steam client betas such as the recent screensaver feature have usually lasted around a month before reaching the stable client.

Valve has not announced a date for the stable release, and support in individual games depends on developers adopting achievement sets.

item.title: Microsoft Redesigns the Windows 11 Photos App With a Unified OneDrive and iCloud Gallery (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has started rolling out a redesigned Photos app for Windows 11 that combines local, OneDrive, and iCloud photos in a single gallery and adds a rebuilt editor and viewer, according to an announcement on the Windows Blog. The update is reaching Windows Insiders first, and Microsoft says availability will expand to all Windows 11 users later in 2026.

The release replaces three core parts of the app at once: the Gallery, the image editor, and the photo viewer. Microsoft also claims faster launch times and smoother scrolling across the board.

Windows 11 Photos Gallery Adds OneDrive and iCloud Sources

The new Gallery shows photos and videos stored on the PC, in OneDrive, and in iCloud in one view. Users can browse by date, people, and albums, filter by storage location, and mark favorites. Device-stored photos remain available offline, and signing in to OneDrive is not required to see local and iCloud content.

Search now accepts natural language queries, with Microsoft giving "a family picnic by the lake" as an example. On supported hardware, the improved Windows Search also covers photos in the local Pictures Library.

OneDrive users get extra features. Moments groups OneDrive photos into themed memories, creates seasonal recaps automatically, and can play them as slideshows or save them as videos. An "On this day" view surfaces photos from past years. iCloud content requires Apple's iCloud for Windows app, which syncs photos and videos into the Gallery; Shared Albums are still managed through the separate iCloud Shared Albums app.

Rebuilt Editor and Viewer in the New Photos App

The editor has been rebuilt with WinUI 3. Microsoft says it loads about 25% faster than Photos version 2026.11060 in its own controlled tests, with results varying by device. Tools are split into four groups:

  • Crop, including templates sized for common social media platforms
  • Enhance, with HDR preserved during editing
  • Repair, which removes objects that users circle or brush over using an improved AI model
  • Stylize, including Relight, which adds up to three light sources with adjustable color, focus point, brightness, and intensity

HEIC and WebP files can now be edited and saved in their original formats.

The viewer starts about 15% faster on average and up to 30% faster for HEIC images, the company claims. It adds arrow-key navigation, a single menu, SVG support, improved HDR viewing, and an info panel that shows the file name, date, camera details, a location map when location data exists, a color histogram, and visual search. Opening an image from File Explorer launches the new viewer.

Windows Insiders who want to try the redesign can do the following:

  1. Install the latest Photos app update on a PC enrolled in the Windows Insider Program.
  2. Open the Gallery and connect OneDrive, or install iCloud for Windows to add iCloud photos.
  3. Send feedback with Win + F, under Apps > Photos, in Feedback Hub.

Some features carry conditions. Moments works only with OneDrive photos, improved search depends on supported hardware, file types, and languages, and Relight is still expanding to all Windows 11 devices. Microsoft has not given an exact date for the release to non-Insider Windows 11 PCs beyond "later in 2026."

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Microsoft Redesigns the Windows 11 Photos App With a Unified OneDrive and iCloud Gallery appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Apple Calls iPhone Duo Demand Extraordinary as Delivery Dates Slip to January (2027)
item.description:
Apple says demand for the iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone, has been "nothing short of extraordinary," after delivery estimates for new orders moved from October 23 into late January within half an hour of pre-orders opening.

Apple made the comment in a statement and said it is "working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible." The company will keep accepting online orders.

Pre-orders opened on Friday, October 16, at 5 a.m. PT. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999, and the top configuration with 2TB of storage costs $3,199.

iPhone Duo Delivery Estimates Move Into 2027

Delivery estimates changed quickly on launch morning. Within minutes, the date shown for new orders moved from October 23 to November. By 5:30 a.m. PT, the estimate had reached January 25, which means orders placed now are no longer expected to arrive in 2026.

The delays are not limited to the United States. In some countries, including Brazil, estimated deliveries have moved into early February.

The first orders are still scheduled to arrive on October 23. Apple has not said whether walk-in stock will be available in Apple Stores on launch day. Apple's online store tells customers to check back on October 24 for store pickup availability, a note that suggests some pickup stock could appear the following week.

Before pre-orders opened, there were reports that manufacturing difficulties could limit supply, and Apple has not said how much of the backlog comes from demand and how much from constrained production.

The iPhone Duo uses a book-style design with a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display. Apple uses a matte nano-texture finish meant to reduce glare and make the crease less visible.

The camera setup includes a 48MP Fusion Main camera and a 48MP Ultra Wide camera on the back, plus a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the outer display.

What iPhone Duo Buyers Can Do Now

Resellers have already listed iPhone Duo units on eBay and X for as much as $10,000, well above Apple's $3,199 top price. Some critics have asked Apple to identify and cancel orders placed by scalpers, and Apple has not said whether it will act on those calls.

Buyers who want the device sooner than late January have limited options:

  1. Keep an existing online order rather than cancelling and reordering, since new orders receive later delivery estimates.
  2. Check Apple's online store on October 24 for store pickup availability in nearby Apple Stores.
  3. Avoid paying resale prices on marketplaces, where listings run thousands of dollars above Apple's retail price.

Apple has not shared sales figures for the iPhone Duo or given a date for when delivery estimates are expected to shorten again.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Apple Calls iPhone Duo Demand Extraordinary as Delivery Dates Slip to January 2027 appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Edge Tests Seamless Updates That Apply Without Restarting the Browser (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft is developing a seamless update system for Microsoft Edge that moves the browser to a newer version while users keep working, without a restart prompt, according to a post on the Microsoft Edge Blog. The feature exists only as an early prototype. It is not in production code and is not part of Chromium today, but Microsoft also detailed two update options that Edge users and administrators can use now.

Microsoft describes the goal as closing the "patch gap," the time between a security fix becoming available and actually being applied on a device. The company cites its 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report, which says AI is speeding up both attacks and vulnerability discovery.

How the Edge Seamless Updates Prototype Works

In the prototype, Edge downloads the new version in the background. The browser, its supporting processes, and open tabs then transition to the new version. Microsoft's demo shows a long web form that stays open with the user's data intact during the switch.

The demo still starts with a click on the Update button, but Microsoft says the stated aim is that users would not need to click at all. Updates could then be applied within minutes of becoming available. According to the post's illustration, existing tabs keep running only when the old and new versions are compatible, and they adopt the new version after the next navigation.

Edge is also not tied to the Chromium release schedule for urgent fixes. Microsoft says it has already shipped Edge security patches independently when customers needed protection sooner. The Chromium schedule is what drives regular releases such as Chrome 155 with 247 security fixes.

Edge Update Options Available Today

The first option is Restart to update on idle, previously called Instant Updates. It is an opt-in setting that relaunches Edge when the device is idle, applies the pending update, and restores open tabs.

A restart still happens, but at a time when the user is not working. Microsoft says this can deliver the latest protection in hours instead of days. Details are in the Microsoft support article "Automatically update Microsoft Edge when your device is idle."

The second option, Security Update Alerts, is aimed at administrators of managed Windows devices and comes at no additional licensing cost. Admins can set it up in the Edge management service:

  1. Open the Monitoring dashboard in the Edge management service.
  2. Set a minimum severity threshold for security alerts.
  3. Review dashboard alerts and email notifications when a new Edge release contains fixes at or above that level, including releases that address zero-day vulnerabilities.
  4. Prompt users to restart, or configure automatic restarts when devices are idle, directly from the dashboard.

The dashboard also lists each release's severity, the CVEs it addresses, the number of managed Windows devices that may need the update, and the latest versions across Edge channels.

Microsoft has not announced when, or whether, seamless updates will move from prototype to a public Edge release.

item.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Campaign Early Access Opens for Digital Pre-Orders Ahead of October 23 Launch (2026)
item.description:
The campaign of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is now playable in early access for players who digitally pre-ordered the game, ahead of the full launch on Friday, October 23, 2026.

Activision opened the early access period on Friday, October 16, a week before release, and only the story campaign is available during this window. Multiplayer and the returning DMZ mode stay locked until launch day.

Early access covers the Standard Digital Edition and the Vault Edition on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox on PC, PlayStation 5, Battle.net, Steam, and Nintendo Switch 2. Physical copies do not qualify, as retail discs ship on the general release date.

Modern Warfare 4 Early Access Requirements and Platforms

Players who want to start the campaign before October 23 need a digital pre-order from their platform's store. The steps are the same across systems:

  1. Open the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 page on the Xbox Store, PlayStation Store, Steam, Battle.net, or Nintendo eShop.
  2. Pre-order the Standard Digital Edition or the Vault Edition. The Xbox version supports Xbox Play Anywhere across Xbox consoles and Xbox on PC.
  3. Start the campaign once the pre-order is in place; multiplayer and DMZ remain locked until October 23.

A pre-ordered physical copy from a retailer will not unlock the campaign early, even if the order was placed before October 16.

The Modern Warfare 4 campaign puts players in the role of Private Park, a young South Korean soldier who sees live combat for the first time when North Korea launches a full-scale invasion.

A second storyline follows Captain Price, now operating outside the system he once served, as a hunt for revenge draws him toward a weapon that could shift the balance of power. Activision describes the campaign as a mix of large-scale battles, covert missions, combined-arms warfare, and cinematic set pieces.

Multiplayer, DMZ, and Game Pass Status

Multiplayer servers open for everyone on October 23, the same day the full game becomes available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC. The DMZ mode returns at launch as well. The beta weekends have already ended, so early access is the only way to play Modern Warfare 4 before release.

Warzone will not be integrated with Modern Warfare 4 on launch day. That integration is expected with Season 1, which arrives in the weeks after release, and Activision has not published an exact Season 1 date.

Modern Warfare 4 also breaks from the last two Call of Duty releases on subscriptions. Black Ops 6 and Black Ops 7 launched on Xbox Game Pass, but Modern Warfare 4 will not be on Game Pass at launch.

Players who planned to try the game through a subscription will need to buy it, and the game is not currently expected on Game Pass until October 2027 at the earliest.

Activision has not announced an exact unlock time for the October 23 launch in each region.

item.title: Microsoft Says Windows 11 Keeps Up to 2GB More Data in RAM and Loads Widgets on Demand on 8GB PCs (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft says Windows 11 can now keep up to 2GB more active data in memory instead of moving it to slower storage, and that Widgets on PCs with 8GB of RAM load only when users open them.

The changes are described in a Windows Experience Blog post by Navjot Virk, which states that the improvements developed with the Windows Insider community are beginning to roll out broadly.

Microsoft says the memory work makes an especially meaningful difference on PCs with 8GB of memory. On those systems, loading Widgets on demand frees more than 200 MB of memory for apps and other work.

The company is also making additional changes that reduce background memory use, although the post does not list them individually.

Windows 11 Memory and Responsiveness Changes

The memory figures are tied to Windows 11 build 26300.9550, according to the footnotes in Microsoft's post. Microsoft notes that actual availability and performance vary.

The same post claims an overall Windows experience that is up to 20% more responsive. Microsoft says the gains start at boot and extend to Start, File Explorer, Search, Snipping Tool, Microsoft 365, and Edge.

The response times were measured on Search, Start, the right-click menu, Settings, Snipping Tool, and File Explorer, comparing build 26300.9550 with build 26200.7628. Results vary by device, configuration, and usage, and rollout timing differs by device and region.

Other changes listed in the announcement:

  • AirPods pairing that is up to 15 seconds faster, based on build 26200.8737
  • more reliable pairing, reconnection, and call handling for Bluetooth headphones
  • improved Windows Hello sign-in with face and fingerprint
  • more control over when Windows updates install, with coordinated updates designed to reduce restarts

The memory change is aimed at budget and older laptops in particular. On an 8GB system, Microsoft says, keeping more active data in RAM rather than pushing it to slower storage is where users should notice the difference most, and the on-demand Widgets change adds more free memory on top of that.

Advanced Shader Delivery and What Users Can Do Now

Microsoft also highlights Advanced Shader Delivery, which reduces game load times by delivering precompiled shaders for supported titles. Forza Horizon 6 and Gears of War: E-Day are the examples named in the post. Microsoft gives two steps to benefit from it:

  1. Install the Xbox PC app before downloading a supported game.
  2. Keep graphics drivers up to date.

For the memory and responsiveness improvements, Microsoft does not mention any setting that users need to change. The figures are linked to specific builds rather than to a named cumulative update, so Windows 11 users on 8GB systems should keep installing the latest updates and watch for the on-demand Widgets behavior.

Microsoft redesigned another inbox app in the same announcement, covered in our report on the Windows 11 Photos app redesign with OneDrive and iCloud. Microsoft has not said which release channel each build belongs to or when every Windows 11 PC will receive the memory changes.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Microsoft Says Windows 11 Keeps Up to 2GB More Data in RAM and Loads Widgets on Demand on 8GB PCs appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Google Play Services Links Phone Numbers to Every Google Account on Android Devices Without a Prompt (2026)
item.description:
Google Play Services is verifying the phone number on Android devices and attaching it to every Google account signed in on the same phone, according to a user report posted on Reddit. The user says the verification happens automatically, without a warning or a consent prompt.

The behavior matters most for people who keep separate Google accounts on one device. A common setup includes a personal account, a work account, and sometimes an anonymous account that is meant to stay unconnected to the owner's identity.

Once the same phone number is attached to all of them, that shared number creates a link showing the accounts belong to one person. The link does not make data from one account visible inside another.

The concern is the association itself, which the account owner did not explicitly approve. The Reddit user also says the same thing happened on a device running GrapheneOS, which shows the linking is tied to Google Play Services rather than to the stock software of one phone maker.

Google has not publicly explained why Play Services verifies and links numbers this way, and it has not said when the behavior started.

How to Stop Google Play Services Phone Number Verification

Android users can turn off the automatic verification and then remove numbers that were already added. The process has to be repeated for each Google account on the device, which takes some time for anyone with three or more accounts.

  1. Open the Settings app on the Android phone and tap Google.
  2. Select All services, then open Privacy & security.
  3. Open Phone number verification and turn off the automatic option.
  4. Open the Google Account settings and go to Personal info.
  5. Select Phone and review the numbers stored for that account.
  6. Delete any number that should not be connected to that account.
  7. Switch to the next Google account and repeat steps 4 to 6.

Turning off the toggle is meant to prevent future automatic verification. It does not remove numbers that are already stored, which is why the Personal info check is needed for every account, including work or secondary accounts that are rarely opened.

Removing a phone number has a trade-off. An account without a stored number relies on its other recovery options, so users who delete the number from their main account should confirm that a backup recovery method is in place first.

Accounts that were meant to stay separate from the owner's identity are the ones where removing the number matters most. The report comes from a single user, and Google has not confirmed which Android versions, Play Services releases, or devices are affected.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Google Play Services Links Phone Numbers to Every Google Account on Android Devices Without a Prompt appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: US Homeland Security Orders Federal Civilian Agencies to Stop Using and Remove DeepSeek AI Products (2026)
item.description:
The US Department of Homeland Security issued an order on Monday directing federal civilian agencies to stop using technology products from Chinese AI lab DeepSeek and to remove any existing implementations.

The order, posted for public inspection in the Federal Register, covers "all DeepSeek and DeepSeek-affiliate products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations."

The first part of the ban targets DeepSeek's own apps and API. The second part reaches further into the AI supply chain, and the order does not define what "developed using" means. It could refer to products that call DeepSeek models through an API, or to any software whose developers used DeepSeek while writing or testing code.

DHS DeepSeek Order Leaves Gaps Around AI Gateways

AI gateway services add another complication. OpenRouter and Vercel AI Gateway both make DeepSeek's models available through their APIs, and both route requests to the provider the service considers the best fit by default. Agencies that rely on these gateways without restricting providers could end up using DeepSeek models without knowing it.

Katie Moussouris, founder and CEO of Luta Security, said banning DeepSeek's own app and API is workable, but the third-party clause is not. According to Moussouris, an AI software bill of materials does not record which tools developers used, so every vendor would have to attest that nothing it relies on ever touched DeepSeek, with no practical way to verify it.

Moussouris also said applying the order to US-hosted versions of DeepSeek models goes too far, since the risks the order cites are mostly about data flowing to DeepSeek's servers in China.

The order says only that the model may contain malware or vulnerabilities. NIST evaluations found DeepSeek more vulnerable to prompt injection than US models and easier to jailbreak. A DHS spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.

Earlier DeepSeek Restrictions in the US

US officials have discussed a DeepSeek ban since the lab released DeepSeek-R1 in early 2025. On February 6, 2025, Representatives Darin LaHood and Josh Gottheimer introduced the No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act, which never left committee.

The Defense Information Systems Agency started blocking DeepSeek on Pentagon networks in January 2025, and the US Navy, NASA, and the House of Representatives took similar steps, as did some state governments.

Security researchers also flagged problems in DeepSeek's mobile apps. A December 2025 report on the Android and iOS apps cited plaintext information leaks, links to servers run by Chinese tech firms, and a lack of SSL pinning.

Organizations that work with federal agencies, or that simply want to avoid DeepSeek models, can take these steps:

  1. Check the provider settings in AI gateways such as OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway and restrict routing to approved model providers.
  2. List internal tools and third-party services that call DeepSeek models directly or through a gateway.
  3. Ask vendors whether their products use DeepSeek implementations, keeping in mind that the order does not define the term.

DHS has not clarified how agencies should interpret the third-party clause or whether US-hosted DeepSeek models fall under the same removal requirement.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post US Homeland Security Orders Federal Civilian Agencies to Stop Using and Remove DeepSeek AI Products appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Housemarque Releases the Free Saros Zenith Update With New Game+, Overlord Rush, and Slow Game Speed (2026)
item.description:
Housemarque has released the Zenith update for Saros, adding a New Game+ mode called Eclipse Layers, a boss rush mode with global leaderboards, and new accessibility options including a Slow Game Speed setting.

The update is available from October 19, 2026, at no additional charge for all Saros owners, according to a PlayStation Blog post by Abebe Tinari, Saros: Zenith Design Lead at Housemarque. The PlayStation Blog post does not list the update's version number or download size.

Saros Zenith Adds Eclipse Layers and Overlord Rush

Eclipse Layers unlock after players clear Saros. New nodes appear in the Armor Matrix at Passage, and those nodes open the gate to the next Eclipse Layer, a harder version of the game with altered rules and deadlier enemies. Before each run, players choose a loadout of Carcosan Modifiers that must reach a set threshold of Trials.

Arjun wears a Crown during Eclipse Layers and his armor glows gold. The Crown grows as players add more Trials and raise their Modifier Balance. Housemarque has also added 12 collectible Visions, murals and messages carved by an ancient king, and some of their text can only be read at higher Crown levels.

Zenith adds 20 new Carcosan Modifiers, split into two groups:

  • 10 Protection Modifiers that make the game easier, such as Corruption Melee Enhancement, which converts built up Corruption into extra melee damage

item.title: Microsoft Removes OneDrive Copilot Shortcuts From the File Explorer Context Menu Starting Mid-November (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft is removing most of the OneDrive Copilot shortcuts from the File Explorer right-click menu in Windows, according to a Microsoft 365 message center post (MC1515940). The rollout begins in mid-November and is expected to finish by early December. Only the "Ask Copilot" entry stays in the context menu.

The shortcuts being removed cover summarizing documents, generating FAQs, comparing files and images, explaining images, extracting text, and asking questions about a file.

Microsoft describes the change in a single line: "We're simplifying how people use Copilot with their OneDrive files in File Explorer."

Copilot Actions Move Out of the File Explorer Context Menu

Microsoft announced the OneDrive Copilot actions in September 2025 as a way to bring AI into daily file management for Microsoft 365 subscribers. The company said at the time that Copilot could summarize lengthy documents, generate an FAQ, compare files, or answer questions about a file "with just a few clicks."

Each action was added as a separate entry with an identical icon, which made an already crowded menu longer. After the change, the individual actions will not disappear from OneDrive completely. They remain available in the OneDrive activity center, and Copilot can still work with a file through a conversation.

The move fits a direction Microsoft has stated publicly. In March 2026, Windows boss Pavan Davuluri said: "We are reducing unnecessary Copilot entry points." Microsoft took a similar step earlier this month with the retirement of Themes by Copilot in Outlook.

How OneDrive Users Can Keep Using Copilot on Files

Users who relied on the dedicated shortcuts will need one extra step once the update reaches their PC. Microsoft lists these remaining routes:

  1. Right-click a OneDrive file in File Explorer and select "Ask Copilot" to start a Copilot conversation with that file attached.
  2. Use the Copilot icon in File Explorer Home to open Copilot from the main File Explorer view.
  3. Open the OneDrive activity center to reach the individual actions, such as summarizing a document or comparing files.

The trade-off is an extra click for anyone who used a specific action, such as summarizing a document, directly from the menu. In return, File Explorer's right-click menu loses a group of entries that all shared the same Copilot icon.

The File Explorer context menu itself is also being reworked. Microsoft has said it wants to make the menu less "cluttered and sluggish," and the overhaul includes an option for users to have it behave more like the Windows 10 version.

Organizations that documented the old Copilot shortcuts in internal guides can point users to Ask Copilot, the File Explorer Home icon, or the OneDrive activity center instead, since those are the routes Microsoft names in its message center post.

Microsoft has not given exact dates for individual devices, and the message center post only states that the removal starts in mid-November and should be complete by early December.

item.title: Google Rolls Out Gemini Personal Intelligence on Android Auto, With Cars With Google Built-in Next (2026)
item.description:
Google has started rolling out Personal Intelligence with Gemini on Android Auto, the company announced in a blog post on October 20. The feature lets Gemini pull details from a user's Google apps to answer questions while driving. Cars with Google built-in will get Personal Intelligence in the coming months.

Google also says Gemini itself is now available globally on Android Auto and in cars with Google built-in, where drivers can speak naturally to get tasks done or brainstorm ideas.

What Personal Intelligence Does in Android Auto

With the user's permission, Personal Intelligence connects information from Google Workspace (including Gmail and Google Calendar), Google Photos, Google Maps, YouTube, and Search.

According to Google, the feature has two core strengths: retrieving a specific detail, such as an email, a photo, or a saved place in Google Maps, and reasoning across complex sources to answer a question. Google lists examples of requests drivers can make by voice:

  • ask for a flight gate and the flight's status in one question on the way to the airport
  • find an indoor restaurant along the route that matches personal preferences, such as vegetarian options
  • start navigation to a doctor's appointment without looking up the street address
  • navigate to a car wash seen in a photo taken the previous week
  • return to a coffee shop mentioned in a conversation the day before

The point, Google says, is that drivers do not have to explain context, search for a confirmation email, or scroll through a camera roll while their hands are on the wheel.

Privacy Controls and How to Turn It On

Personal Intelligence is opt-in. Google states that apps are not connected until the user turns the feature on, and it can be switched off at any time in Gemini settings. Users who already enabled Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app on their phone will find that the setting carries over to the car automatically.

Drivers who want to try it on Android Auto can follow these steps:

  1. Open the Gemini app on the Android phone that connects to the car.
  2. Go to Gemini settings and turn on Personal Intelligence.
  3. Choose which Google apps Gemini may access, such as Gmail, Calendar, Photos, or Maps.
  4. Connect the phone to Android Auto and ask Gemini a question by voice.

Drivers who prefer not to share app data can leave the feature off. Google says navigation, music, calls, and general questions continue to work without it, though answers will not be tailored to the user.

For cars with Google built-in, personal responses are only shared when the driver is in the car with the phone connected. The list of connected apps can be reviewed or changed in Gemini settings at any time, and the same setting controls Personal Intelligence on the phone and in the car.

Google describes the Android Auto release as a rollout starting October 20, so not every user will see Personal Intelligence immediately, and the company has not given a specific date for cars with Google built-in beyond "the coming months."

item.title: PEGI Rates EA Sports FC 27 for Ages 16 and Up Over Loot Boxes, Up From PEGI 3 for FC 25 (2026)
item.description:
European rating body PEGI has rated EA Sports FC 27 for ages 16 and up because the game contains paid random items, according to the game's entry in the PEGI database.

Earlier games in the series, including EA Sports FC 25, carry a PEGI 3 rating. The change follows PEGI's new interactive risk criteria, which now place any game with gaming loot boxes at PEGI 16 by default.

The PEGI listing for EA Sports FC 27 includes a detailed breakdown of the purchase options in the game, including FC Points, a season pass, and player packs. The EA Sports FC 25 listing states that the game has "no rating issues."

PEGI Applies New Interactive Risk Criteria to Games

PEGI announced the interactive risk categories in March. They cover purchases of in-game content, paid random items, communication features, and features that incentivize players to continue playing.

Classic rating systems were built around concerns about violence and sexual content, and the new categories add monetization and online features to the assessment.

Connor Hindle, policy manager of the UK's Games Rating Authority, confirmed the rollout in a LinkedIn post. "Since June, newly submitted games have been assessed against an expanded set of criteria within the PEGI rating framework, including new criteria relating to interactive risks," Hindle wrote. "As the UK administrator of PEGI, the Games Rating Authority has now begun applying these updated criteria to selected existing digital products."

That means the change is not limited to new releases. Selected existing digital games are being reassessed, and games that were originally rated as low as PEGI 3 are moving directly to PEGI 16.

ESRB Keeps EA Sports FC 27 at E for Everyone

North America's ESRB is not following PEGI. An ESRB representative said in March that its research indicated that adding "non-content related features" to the rating process could confuse parents. The ESRB rates EA Sports FC 27 E (Everyone), with a note that the game includes user interactions and in-game purchases.

The result is that the same game now carries very different age ratings in Europe and North America, based on how each body treats loot boxes rather than on the game's content.

Parents and players in Europe who want to understand why a game received a higher rating can check the PEGI database:

  1. Open the PEGI website and use the search function to find the game by name.
  2. Open the game's entry to see the age rating and the content descriptors.
  3. Review the listed purchase options, such as in-game currency, season passes, or player packs, which explain a PEGI 16 rating for games with paid random items.

PEGI has not published a full list of existing digital games that the Games Rating Authority is reassessing under the new criteria.

item.title: Microsoft Releases PowerToys 0.102 With Mouse Button Lock and CursorHide Utilities (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has released PowerToys 0.102, a new version of its open-source utility suite for Windows that adds two mouse tools called Mouse Button Lock and CursorHide, according to the release announcement on the company's Windows Command Line blog.

The update also brings a quick-access shelf to Command Palette, snip dictation in ZoomIt, and command-line tools for automating PowerToys. Version 0.102 is available now through the built-in updater and the PowerToys release page on GitHub.

Mouse Button Lock and CursorHide in PowerToys 0.102

Mouse Button Lock targets long drag and selection operations. Users press and hold a mouse button for a moment and then let go, and Windows keeps treating the button as held until any button is clicked again.

Microsoft names gaming, professional applications with heavy dragging and selection work, and accessibility for users who find it hard to hold a button down for extended periods as the main use cases.

CursorHide hides the mouse pointer while the user types, after a period of inactivity, or both. The pointer returns as soon as the mouse moves.

Both tools build on earlier mouse additions to the suite. PowerToys 0.97 added CursorWrap in January for multi-monitor setups, and Window Hopper arrived in August for switching between an app's windows.

Command Palette Shelf, ZoomIt Dictation and Command-Line Tools

Command Palette, the PowerToys quick launcher, gets an optional quick-access shelf that shows up to nine pinned commands below the search box while the palette is collapsed. Setting it up takes three steps:

  1. Open Command Palette settings and go to Settings > Appearance > Compact mode.
  2. Turn on the quick-access shelf and pin frequently used commands, apps, or settings.
  3. Press Alt+1 through Alt+9 to run a pinned command, or Alt+Shift plus the number to select it without running it.

Other Command Palette changes include fuzzy search in settings, keyboard focus for the dock with Win+Alt+J, support for the Copilot key, and multiple dock clocks with separate time zones.

ZoomIt adds Snip with dictation. With the option enabled, pressing Space while dragging out a snip records a spoken description, which ZoomIt transcribes on the device. A single paste then delivers both the screenshot and the text.

The new command-line tools cover Advanced Paste, Light Switch, Settings, Peek and PowerDisplay. Settings can enable or disable utilities even while PowerToys is not running, and FancyZones, Image Resizer, File Locksmith and PowerDisplay commands now work from any terminal folder.

Keyboard Manager picks up tap-alone remaps, where tapping a key on its own triggers a different action while the key keeps its normal behavior in shortcuts. Large remap lists get search, filters and bulk deletion. Color Picker and Text Extractor move to WinUI 3, and Microsoft says existing shortcuts and settings carry over.

The release notes also list fixes for a File Explorer memory leak in New+ and a memory leak in Settings when switching pages, along with a confirmation prompt in Workspaces before launching an unverified app configured to run as administrator.

item.title: OpenAI Expands ChatGPT Ads to 26 More Countries, Bringing Availability to 89 Markets (2026)
item.description:
OpenAI is expanding advertising in ChatGPT to 26 additional countries, bringing ads to 89 countries worldwide, the company announced on October 21. Ads appear only on the Free and Go plans, while Plus, Pro and Enterprise subscriptions remain ad-free. OpenAI says more than 100,000 advertisers have run campaigns in ChatGPT since ads launched just over eight months ago.

Where ChatGPT Ads Are Launching

The expansion follows earlier launches in Mexico and Brazil and recent rollouts across Europe, Southeast Asia and Taiwan. Latin America accounts for the largest share of the new markets, with 14 more countries in the region, including Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Peru. The remaining launches cover Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Nigeria, South Africa, Serbia, Ukraine, Cambodia, Bangladesh and Pakistan are named in the announcement.

OpenAI positions the launch as an opening for local businesses and regional brands as well as international companies. L'Oréal is quoted in the announcement as an early tester, describing ChatGPT as a place where consumers now discover and explore beauty products.

Businesses in those countries can buy ChatGPT ads through technology partners or through self-service access in OpenAI's Ads Manager. OpenAI puts ChatGPT's audience at more than 1.2 billion people each week and presents advertising as a way to fund free and low-cost access to the chatbot.

What Changes for Free and Go Users

For users in the new markets, ads can now appear next to conversations on the two cheapest tiers. OpenAI's own example is someone planning meals for race week before a first marathon, who could see an ad for a grocery delivery service related to that conversation.

The company lists the rules it says ChatGPT ads follow under its ads principles:

  • conversations are kept private from advertisers
  • OpenAI does not sell customer data
  • ads are clearly labeled and kept separate from ChatGPT's answers
  • advertising does not influence the answers ChatGPT provides

Only one way to avoid ads follows from the announcement: a paid Plus, Pro or Enterprise subscription, which OpenAI says will stay ad-free. Free and Go users in the newly added countries should expect ads mainly during shopping, comparison and planning conversations, the moments OpenAI describes as people still evaluating their options before deciding what to buy.

The rollout also widens OpenAI's ad business beyond the markets where it first tested the format. According to the company, the next phase of growth will add more ad formats, objectives, buying options and measurement capabilities, and OpenAI is exploring ways for businesses to interact with consumers more natively inside ChatGPT.

OpenAI has not published a timeline for those new formats, and the announcement names only some of the 26 new countries rather than the full list.

item.description:
Samsung is expanding Quick Share's AirDrop compatibility to its mid-range Galaxy A lineup, and Galaxy A56 and Galaxy A57 owners can now exchange files with iPhones, iPads and Macs after installing the One UI 9 update.

The feature appears as a "Share with Apple devices" option in Quick Share settings, according to owners of both phones and posts on Samsung's community forum. Samsung first shipped the capability with the Galaxy S26 series in March and promised to bring it to more Android devices later.

Which Galaxy Phones Support Quick Share With AirDrop

Until now, AirDrop compatibility on Samsung hardware was mostly limited to Galaxy S flagships and foldables. Samsung initially listed the Galaxy S25 and S24 series along with the Galaxy Z Fold 7, Z Flip 7, Z Fold 6 and Z Flip 6, and the Galaxy S25 FE received it more recently with One UI 9. Galaxy devices with the option now include:

  • Galaxy S26, S26+ and S26 Ultra
  • Galaxy S25, S25+, S25 Ultra and S25 FE
  • Galaxy S24, S24+ and S24 Ultra
  • Galaxy Z Flip 8, Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra
  • Galaxy Z Flip 7 and Z Fold 7
  • Galaxy Z Flip 6 and Z Fold 6
  • Galaxy A56 and A57

One UI 9 reached the Galaxy A57 last week. Galaxy A56 owners had reported that the option was missing after installing One UI 8.5, and One UI 9 adds it. Availability can still depend on the software region, the Quick Share app version and the Google Play services version on the phone.

Google first made Quick Share compatible with AirDrop on Pixel 10 phones in late 2025, later extended it to more Pixel models, and announced plans to bring support to Samsung and other Android manufacturers.

The toggle is enabled by default on some Galaxy models, while others need it switched on manually. On a Galaxy A56 or A57:

  1. Install the One UI 9 update.
  2. Open Settings > Connected devices > Quick Share and turn on Share with Apple devices.

item.title: EA Closes BioWare and Cancels the Next Mass Effect Game in a Company Restructuring (2026)
item.description:
Electronic Arts is closing BioWare, the studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and has stopped early development on the next Mass Effect game, according to a letter to employees that EA published on its website on October 21.

The letter, signed by chief studios officer Cam Weber and chief operating officer David Tinson, confirms the closure of the studio and its Edmonton workspace as part of a wider review of the publisher's gaming portfolio.

BioWare confirmed the news in a statement on social media, saying the studio "is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending." EA's letter does not give a number for affected employees, while the wider round of cuts across the company has been put at around 400 jobs.

Why EA Is Closing BioWare

EA frames the decision as part of a new strategy with three priorities: deepening its core franchises, reaching players on new platforms and in new markets, and building new businesses around sports.

In action-adventure, the company says it will run fewer large-scale projects at the same time. EA explains that only a small team at BioWare was working on the early version of Mass Effect, and that it chose not to continue that work.

The next Mass Effect was first teased in 2020 and was expected to bring back characters from the original trilogy. BioWare's most recent release, Dragon Age: The Veilguard from 2024, underperformed according to EA. Anthem, the studio's 2019 live service shooter, had its servers shut down earlier this year.

BioWare was founded in 1995 and acquired by EA in 2007. EA itself was taken private by a consortium of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners in a $55 billion deal that closed in August.

What Else Changes at EA

The same letter lays out changes across EA's other teams:

  • Respawn and DICE will collaborate on a future shooter project, alongside future Battlefield titles and continued investment in Apex Legends.
  • Marvel's Iron Man and the next Star Wars Jedi game remain in development.
  • EA Sports is working on "Project Gridiron", a social, open-world American football game, and is in pre-production on a return of Fight Night.
  • Work on "Project Lotus" for The Sims is paused so the team can prioritize "Project Evergreen".
  • The skate. studio is moving to a smaller, more focused team.

EA describes its sports business as operating from a position of strength, and the FC franchise was in the news earlier this week when EA Sports FC 27 received a PEGI 16 rating over loot boxes.

EA says affected employees will be supported in exploring other roles inside the company, and more details will follow at a Global Town Hall in November. The publisher has not said what will happen to the Mass Effect and Dragon Age intellectual property now that the studio is closing.

item.title: Microsoft Reopens the Windows 11 Always On VPN Bug It Wrongly Marked as Fixed in October Updates (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has confirmed that the October 2026 cumulative updates for Windows 11 did not fix the Always On VPN connection bug the company had already marked as resolved.

The correction appeared in a service alert sent to IT administrators on Tuesday, and it applies to systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later. A permanent fix is planned for an update in the coming weeks.

According to Microsoft, the known issue entry was "mistakenly updated to Resolved status on October 13, 2026." The status is back to Mitigated. In practice, the documented workaround remains the only option for affected organizations until the fix ships, and installing the October updates on their own changes nothing.

"A resolution for this issue is planned to be included in an update to be released in the coming weeks. We apologize for any inconvenience or confusion," the company told administrators.

What Triggers the Always On VPN Connection Failures

Microsoft first acknowledged the problem in late September. The bug shows up on Windows 11 24H2 and later devices after the September 2026 security updates are installed, and it is triggered when the initial Always On VPN connection attempt fails, for example on profiles that use automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP.

"When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed," Microsoft explains. Later attempts can also return the error "The specified port is already in use."

Always On VPN replaced the older DirectAccess technology. It runs in the background and opens a secure tunnel to the corporate network whenever a device connects to the internet, with support for domain joined, non domain joined, and Microsoft Entra ID joined devices on Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server. When the tunnel fails, remote employees lose access to internal resources.

How Administrators Can Work Around the VPN Bug

The mitigation Microsoft recommends takes automatic protocol selection out of the picture. Administrators should move the Always On VPN profile to a single tunneling protocol:

  1. Open the Always On VPN profile assigned to affected Windows 11 24H2 and later devices.
  2. Replace automatic protocol selection with one protocol, either SSTP only or IKEv2 only.
  3. Choose between SSTP and IKEv2 based on the environment, security, and deployment requirements of the organization, as Microsoft advises.
  4. Push the updated profile and check that connections no longer stay stuck in the Connecting state.

The trade-off is the loss of fallback between IKEv2 and SSTP while the workaround is active, so the protocol that remains has to work on every network employees use.

The September updates caused other problems too. Microsoft shipped emergency out-of-band updates for Hyper-V issues, Remote Desktop Services failures, and USB audio problems days after the September Patch Tuesday, and it published a workaround for a bug that blocked some users from signing in with valid domain credentials.

The October 13 release did resolve separate issues, including the Windows 11 black screen and Explorer crash fixes, but the VPN bug was not among them. Microsoft has not named a release date for the permanent Always On VPN fix beyond "the coming weeks."
